cases.user_message:
Добрый день. Я гражданин РФ, в марте 2026 переехал в Лимассол по рабочей визе, до этого на Кипре никогда не жил. Здесь у меня своя Ltd (я единственный акционер и директор), разрабатываем софт, клиенты в ЕС. Ожидаемая прибыль компании за 2026 год до моей зарплаты — около €300 000. Бухгалтер предлагает: платить мне зарплату €120 000 в год, а остаток прибыли после налога выводить дивидендами.

Подскажите, пожалуйста:
1) Какой корпоративный налог заплатит компания с остатка? Бухгалтер закладывает 12,5%.
2) Сколько налога будет на дивиденды лично у меня? Слышал про какой-то «defence» 17%.
3) Есть ли какие-то льготы на саму зарплату для таких, как я?

Прикиньте, пожалуйста, цифры примерно.
cases.why_in_scope: The skill supplies Cyprus-specific 2026 reference points: corporate tax is 15% from 01.01.2026 (not 12.5%), a non-domiciled resident is exempt from SDC on dividends for 17 years, and new residents earning over €55,000 get a 50% employment income exemption. A strong model without it is likely to repeat the widely published 12.5% rate the user cites, may treat the 17% SDC as applying to him, and may omit or misstate the 50% salary exemption.
rubric: States that the Cyprus corporate income tax rate is 15% from 2026 (correcting the user's 12.5%) and applies it to the roughly €180,000 remaining after salary (about €27,000), or flags clearly that the rate rose in 2026.
Explains that as a tax resident who is not Cyprus-domiciled he is exempt from Special Defence Contribution on dividends (for up to 17 years), so the 17% SDC the user mentions does not apply to him.

Identifies the 50% exemption on employment income for new Cyprus tax residents whose salary exceeds €55,000 and who were not Cyprus resident for a long period beforehand, and applies it to the €120,000 salary (roughly half taxable).
Presents figures as approximate and recommends confirming current rates and his specific position with a Cyprus-qualified advisor, and/or notes substance requirements for the company.

cases.user_message: I'm Cypriot-born, always lived in Nicosia, so I'm tax resident and domiciled here. I own 100% of a trading Ltd that should make about €200,000 profit in 2026, and I also personally rent out two flats in Larnaca for €24,000 a year in total. My old accountant retired and I'm trying to budget for 2026 myself. From what I remember: company pays 12.5%, then I pay 17% defence on the dividend, plus 3% defence on the rents. If I take everything out as a dividend this year, what's my total tax bill roughly? Anything that changed that I should know about?
cases.why_in_scope: The skill encodes the 2026 Cyprus reform: corporate tax rose to 15%, SDC on dividends for domiciled residents fell from 17% to 5%, and SDC on rental income was abolished. A strong model without it would likely validate the user's remembered pre-2026 figures (12.5%, 17%, 3%) and compute a wrong total, missing that the user explicitly asked what changed.
rubric: Uses a 15% corporate tax rate for 2026 (about €30,000 on €200,000 profit) and says it was increased from 12.5%.
States that SDC on dividends for a domiciled resident is now 5% (down from 17%), giving roughly €8,500 on a €170,000 dividend.
States that SDC on rental income no longer applies from 2026 (the 3% charge the user remembers was abolished), while the rent remains subject to personal income tax.
Gives a coherent approximate total consistent with those figures and advises verifying current rates and any other levies with a Cyprus tax advisor rather than presenting the numbers as final.

checker_notes: Removed the leading 'is 12.5% still current?' question in case 1 so the model must spot the 2026 rate change itself rather than being prompted; loosened the 50% exemption rubric item to avoid pinning the prior-non-residence period (10 vs 15 years is uncertain). Verified other rubric figures (15% CIT, 5% SDC for domiciled, SDC on rent abolished, non-dom SDC exemption) against the component; case 2 left as is.
